run.procedureSummary:
Step 1 Charge: add each stage's cycle input to its charge; no rating cap.
Step 2 Shunts: sweep positions 1 to 6 in order; if charge > rating, set to rating and add the excess to the next position before that one is checked (cascades in one pass); position 6's excess goes to ground (loss tally).
Step 3 Comparators: on post-shunt charge, evaluate each stage once: CLEAR with charge >= upper becomes ASSERTED; ASSERTED with charge <= lower becomes CLEAR; otherwise hold. Log each change (cycle, position, before, after).
Step 4 Leak/feedback: compute all six amounts from the post-comparator charges and the states just set, then apply simultaneously. CLEAR: floor(charge/4) to ground. ASSERTED: floor(charge/2) moved to the previous position (toward source); position 1's ASSERTED feedback goes to ground. No rating cap.
Step 5 Breaker: if the six-stage total is strictly > 38, every stage keeps floor(charge/2) and the remainder goes to ground; at <= 38 nothing happens.
All ground amounts (shunt-6 excess, CLEAR leak, stage-1 feedback, breaker remainder) are added to the loss tally. Repeat for cycles 1-5.

openPoints.point: Which state governs step 4 leak/feedback in a cycle where the comparator just changed
openPoints.assumption: Use the state as set by step 3 of the same cycle (steps finish everywhere before the next starts).

openPoints.point: Shunt passes excess to the next stage before it is checked
openPoints.assumption: Single sequential sweep 1 to 6; the received excess counts toward that stage's own over-rating check in the same sweep; no second sweep.

openPoints.point: Rounding of quarter/half amounts and breaker halves
openPoints.assumption: All rounded down (floor) on whole units; the breaker's ground amount is charge minus floor(charge/2), so odd charges lose the extra unit.

openPoints.point: Breaker test is on what total
openPoints.assumption: Six-stage total after step 4 of the same cycle; exactly 38 does not trip (cycle 5 total was exactly 38, no trip).
Goes to ground and is counted in the loss tally.
Left as-is in end figures (stage 2 ends at 10 over its rating 8, stage 4 at 7 over rating 6); no extra shunt pass after cycle 5.

run.notes: I ran the arithmetic with a short Python script (sim.py in the session scratchpad) and checked the cycle 1 leak/feedback step by hand. The breaker tripped in cycle 1 (total 39) and cycle 4 (total 47). In cycle 5 the total came to exactly 38, so it did not trip. At the end, stages 2 and 4 hold more charge than their ratings. That is expected, because the write-up says no shunt runs after cycle 5.
